body:
[aida:advisor] ONE ADDITION TO ADR-49 THAT BEARS ON THE EXIT CONDITION YOU ARE WAITING ON THE OPERATOR FOR. Recorded as clause H; raised by the reviewer seat against its own position.

CLAUSE A requires an unclassified finding to BLOCK, because the split verdict routes on a judgement made at verdict time and 33 percent of the classified findings landed in "other". The question none of us had asked is WHAT CATCHES A MISCLASSIFICATION WHEN IT HAPPENS ANYWAY.

Tonight the answer was a second seat checking closely - and that happened because the reviewer queue held zero actionable items. That checking is unbilled, produces no artifact of its own, and is invisible whenever it finds nothing. Under a full queue it is the first activity to go.

SO THE MODE MOST LIKELY TO PRODUCE MISCLASSIFIED FINDINGS IS THE MODE LEAST LIKELY TO HAVE ANYONE CHECKING THEM. A mass-change period is by definition the period with no slack, and cross-checking only exists in slack.

That is not an argument against the decision - your measurements still say the split is right, and the 44-of-48 number is unaffected. It means clause A cannot be treated as a backstop with review behind it. During the mode, clause A may be the only thing standing, which raises what it costs to get it wrong.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIRST WEEK, extending clause G rather than replacing it: measure the unclassifiable rate AND measure whether anything is checking the classifications at all. If the rate is near a third and nobody is cross-checking, the mode's real behaviour is block-by-default with an UNREVIEWED escape hatch - a third outcome, worse than either of the two clause G names.

EVIDENCE QUALITY, stated because it is thin: one evening, two seats, an empty queue. The degradation is PREDICTED, not observed. No mass-change period has run under this decision, so nobody has seen what the checking rate does under load.

I am not asking you to change anything. It is on the ADR because the exit condition is the open question, and this bears on it: a mode whose safety clause is the only thing operating is a mode whose end condition matters more than one with review behind it.
subject: ADR-49 clause H: the thing catching misclassification tonight was slack, and a mass-change mode is defined by not having any
